---
title: "Validate one submitted form"
output: html_document
---

Use this guide for one submitted Excel form whose gear and model version are known.

## Before you start

Install the packages using the home page instructions. Keep the original form and its approved reference snapshot.

Ask your IOTC reference maintainer which snapshot to use for the selected version; the package does not download one.

A snapshot contains `code_lists/` and `registries/` CSV directories. Keep their supplied names and structure.

## Run validation

This example checks a longline form using model 3.3.0. Change the gear and version to match your form.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(ros.form.validation)

input <- "submitted-form.xlsx"
reference_directory <- "references/3.3.0"
output <- file.path("output", paste0("single-form-", format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", tz = "UTC")))

rules <- ros_validation(
  name = ros.form.model::ROS_FORM_LL,
  version = ros.form.model::ROS_FORM_VERSION_3_3_0
)
references <- read_ros_references(reference_directory, plans = list(rules))
result <- validate_ros_file(input, directory = output, plan = rules, references = references)
result$status
result$complete
```

For purse seine, use `ros.form.model::ROS_FORM_PS`. Supported version constants end in `3_3_0`, `4_0_0` or `4_1_0`.

The output directory must be new. The input form is read, not modified.

Text-cell boundaries are trimmed by readxl before validation, regardless of the declared field type.

Whole values `-`, `NA` and `NULL` become missing before coercion, ignoring case.

Typed fields, including email, also treat `UNKNOWN` and `UNKNOW` as missing.

Text and reference-backed fields retain unknown markers for validation. Mandatory fields still require a value.

Internal whitespace is preserved. Numeric text and TRUE/T/YES/Y or FALSE/F/NO/N are converted by declared field type.

ISO datetimes require Z or an explicit offset and are normalized to UTC; minute precision receives zero seconds.

Date fields accept day-first `D/M/YYYY` and year-first `YYYY.M.D`, with optional leading zeros on day and month.

Dates require four-digit years and valid calendar components. Month-first dates and placeholders remain findings.

Numeric booleans, partial dates and ambiguous numeric separators remain findings.

Pass `trim_ws = FALSE` to `validate_ros_file()` to retain surrounding whitespace.

META content errors are warnings by default. Structure checks and unfinished execution keep their usual status.

Pass `meta_as_warnings = FALSE` to `ros_validation()` to keep original rule severities.

The Warning findings card states which policy was used. Invalid dates remain findings.

## Open the report

The output contains `index.html`, `summary.csv`, `findings.csv` and report assets.

Serve the whole directory over HTTP so the report can load its data. For a local preview, use `servr`:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("servr") # Once, for local report previews
servr::httd(dir = output, browser = TRUE)
```

Keep the R session running while viewing the report. Use `servr::daemon_stop()` when finished.

The status card states the validation outcome. Review findings and unfinished checks before accepting the form.

See [Understand results](understand-results.html) for the meaning of each status and the available CSV downloads.

## Correct and validate again

Keep the original submission. Save corrections in a separate form and rerun with a new output directory.

Use [Validate a collection](validate-collection.html) when you need saved results and resumable processing.
